% Pocket Dicionario — a modern edition of the cleaned text.
% Generated by tools/pocket.py from work/editions/dicionario.jsonl, the
% same source as the HTML page: the two editions cannot diverge.
\documentclass[9pt]{extarticle}
\usepackage[paperwidth=110mm,paperheight=180mm,
            top=9mm,bottom=11mm,inner=11mm,outer=8mm,
            twoside,includehead,headsep=3mm]{geometry}
\usepackage{fontspec}
\usepackage{multicol}
\usepackage{fancyhdr}
\usepackage{microtype}
\usepackage{xcolor}
\usepackage{needspace}
% Hyphenation: see idopatterns.tex. Neither French nor Esperanto suits
% Ido; the patterns are written for it, and loaded at run time -- which
% LuaTeX allows and pdfTeX does not.
\newlanguage\idolingvo
\language=\idolingvo
\lefthyphenmin=2 \righthyphenmin=3
\input{idopatterns}

\setmainfont{Charis SIL}[Ligatures=TeX, Numbers=OldStyle]
\newfontfamily\titra{Inter}[Ligatures=TeX]

\definecolor{grize}{gray}{0.45}

% Cover, title page and back cover: see cover.tex. That is where the
% azure, #007FFF, is defined.
\input{cover}

% The book has only ONE colour. The accent -- the headwords, the large
% letters, the sub-entries, the square that announces them -- is not one
% colour more: it is the azure of the cover, laid by reference. Written
% that way, it cannot drift.
%
% On white the azure gives 3.83 to 1, a little under the 4.5 a running
% text asks for; but the headword is bold, and blue has long been the
% colour of the words one looks up. In greyscale it falls to 78 %, which
% keeps it darker than the text is light. The brown that preceded it
% stood photocopying better, 90 %, but it made two colours in a book that
% wants only one.
\colorlet{akcento}{idoblua}

\setlength{\columnsep}{4.2mm}
\setlength{\columnseprule}{0.2pt}
\renewcommand{\columnseprulecolor}{\color{grize!45}}
\setlength{\parindent}{0pt}
\setlength{\emergencystretch}{3em}
\hyphenpenalty=200
\tolerance=3000

% --- Running heads -------------------------------------------------------
% LaTeX's own markers (\markboth, \leftmark, \rightmark) do NOT suit here:
% multicol does not assign them reliably across a column break, and page
% 411 showed « zigomorfa », a word that is not on it.
%
% We therefore note the page of each entry in the .aux file, by the same
% mechanism as \label -- the write is deferred to the shipout, so the
% number is exact. The second pass reads that note before setting, and the
% running heads come from it: the FIRST word of the page on the left, the
% LAST on the right. Two passes are therefore needed, which
% tools/all_editions.py does.
\makeatletter
\newcommand\vorpag[2]{%
  \expandafter\gdef\csname pglasta@#2\endcsname{#1}%
  \@ifundefined{pgunesma@#2}%
    {\expandafter\gdef\csname pgunesma@#2\endcsname{#1}}{}}
\newcommand\pgunesma{\@ifundefined{pgunesma@\the\value{page}}{}%
  {\csname pgunesma@\the\value{page}\endcsname}}
\newcommand\pglasta{\@ifundefined{pglasta@\the\value{page}}{}%
  {\csname pglasta@\the\value{page}\endcsname}}
\makeatother
% A blank page inserted by \cleardoublepage carries no folio: in printed
% books the blank pages are mute. LaTeX's original definition leaves the
% current style in force, so the number appeared on the verso of the title.
\makeatletter
\def\cleardoublepage{\clearpage\if@twoside\ifodd\c@page\else
  \null\thispagestyle{empty}\newpage\fi\fi}
\makeatother

\pagestyle{fancy}
\fancyhf{}
\fancyhead[LE]{\titra\footnotesize\bfseries\pgunesma}
\fancyhead[RO]{\titra\footnotesize\bfseries\pglasta}
\fancyhead[C]{\titra\footnotesize\color{grize}\thepage}
\renewcommand{\headrulewidth}{0.3pt}
\renewcommand{\headrule}{\hbox to\headwidth{\color{grize!50}\leaders\hrule height \headrulewidth\hfill}}

% --- Elements of an entry ------------------------------------------------
\makeatletter
\newcommand{\artiklo}[1]{\par\needspace{2\baselineskip}%
  \protected@write\@auxout{}{\string\vorpag{#1}{\thepage}}%
  \hangindent=2.6mm\hangafter=1\relax}
\makeatother
\newcommand{\vorto}[1]{{\titra\bfseries\color{akcento}#1}}
\newcommand{\fako}[1]{\enspace\textit{(#1)}}
\newcommand{\senco}[2]{\enspace{\titra\bfseries\footnotesize #1.}~#2}
\newcommand{\latina}[1]{\enspace\textit{L. #1}}
% The chemical symbol. The label takes the italic, like that of the Latin
% name; the symbol stays UPRIGHT -- a sloped formula reads badly, and the
% italic there means something other than plain emphasis.
\newcommand{\simbolo}[1]{\enspace\textit{Simb. kem.}\,#1}
\newcommand{\lingui}[1]{\enspace{\titra\scriptsize\color{grize}#1}}

% Sub-entry: a phrase the author underlined and which carries its own
% definition -- « Proporciono geometriala: ... ». Drowned in the paragraph,
% it could not be found; it therefore opens its own indented paragraph, the
% phrase in bold and its qualifier in italic, like the domain.
% #1 qualifier (may be empty) · #2 phrase · #3 definition
% A \parbox does not break: in a column of 45 mm, the least long-winded
% definition overflowed. We therefore set an ordinary paragraph, merely
% shifted, which LuaTeX can break and justify like the others.
\newcommand{\subvorto}[5]{\par\nopagebreak
  {\leftskip=2.2mm\relax\hangindent=2.2mm\hangafter=1\relax\noindent
   % A small solid square, drawn with a rule: it depends on no font and on no
% package of symbols, so it cannot go missing.
% A sense with no body of its own -- « analitika » has only its phrases --
% carries its number here rather than alone on an empty line.
   \if\relax\detokenize{#4}\relax\else{\titra\bfseries\footnotesize #4.}~\fi
   \textcolor{akcento}{\rule[0.18ex]{0.9mm}{0.9mm}}\,%
   % BREAKING spaces: with \enspace, the phrase, its qualifier and the start
% of the definition formed one unbreakable block, and the line overflowed
% the column -- 45 mm does not forgive.
% The phrase takes the accent colour, like the headword: the colour says
% « this is to be looked up », the indent says « this depends on the
% entry ». Bold black had more contrast than the accent: the sub-entry
% weighed more than the headword it depends on, which reversed the
% hierarchy. No head of an entry is in bold black any more.
   {\titra\bfseries\color{akcento}#2}%
   \if\relax\detokenize{#1}\relax\else\ \textit{(#1)}\fi
   % An attached entry -- « protestanto » under « protestar » -- keeps its
% language codes: attaching it does not demote it.
   \ #3\if\relax\detokenize{#5}\relax\else\lingui{#5}\fi\par}}

% Each letter opens on a RECTO, as in bound dictionaries: the section is
% found by riffling, without reading. The letter is set large, alone on its
% line, with a rule beneath it.
\makeatletter
\newcommand{\sekciono}[1]{%
  \cleardoublepage
  % The page of the section, noted in the .aux file like the words: the PDF
% bookmarks are built from it, on the second pass.
  \protected@write\@auxout{}{\string\sekpag{#1}{\thepage}}%
  \vspace*{2mm}%
  % The large letter is set in the font of the COVER, not in that of the
% running heads. It is not part of the apparatus -- Inter carries the
% book's apparatus, the running heads, the headwords, the sense numbers,
% the language codes -- but a TITLE: the only sign in the book of the same
% order as the IDO of the cover. It already has its colour; it takes its
% voice too.
%
% The size goes from 34 to 35.34 so that the letter does not shrink: the
% capital height of Jost* is 0.700 em against 0.72754 for Inter, and
% 34 x 0.72754 / 0.700 = 35.34 gives both the same capital, 24.74 pt.
  {\centering\kovrilfonto\bfseries\fontsize{35.34}{38}\selectfont
   \color{akcento}#1\par}%
  \vspace{1.5mm}\hrule height0.5pt\vspace{4mm}}
\makeatother

% --- PDF bookmarks -------------------------------------------------------
% A dictionary of 440 pages is not riffled on a screen. A PDF reader can
% show a side panel of contents: we give it the same hold as the bound
% book -- the twenty-six letters, and under each the word the head of each
% page carries, exactly what the eye looks for in turning the leaves. The
% bookmark of an even page therefore carries its FIRST word, that of an
% odd page its LAST, like the running heads.
%
% They are laid ALL together, just after \begin{document}, from the .aux
% of the previous pass: the PDF format requires the order of the bookmarks
% to follow that of the pages, and laid as the text ran, the letter's and
% the page's disputed the same instant of shipout. Written in one piece,
% the order is that of the loop, and so that of the pages.
\usepackage[hidelinks,bookmarksopen=false,bookmarksdepth=2,
            pdftitle={Dicionario de la 10.000 radiki di la linguo universala Ido},
            pdfauthor={Marcelo Persiko (Marcel Pesch)}]{hyperref}
\usepackage{bookmark}

\makeatletter
\newcommand\sekpag[2]{\expandafter\gdef\csname sek@#2\endcsname{#1}}
\newcommand\finapag[1]{\gdef\fina@pagino{#1}}
\AtEndDocument{\clearpage
  \immediate\write\@auxout{\string\finapag{\the\value{page}}}}
\newcount\pg@nombro
\newcommand\signeti{%
  \@ifundefined{fina@pagino}{}{%
    \pg@nombro=\z@
    \loop\ifnum\pg@nombro<\fina@pagino\relax
      \advance\pg@nombro\@ne
      \@ifundefined{sek@\the\pg@nombro}{}%
        {\bookmark[level=1,page=\the\pg@nombro]%
          {\csname sek@\the\pg@nombro\endcsname}}%
      \ifodd\pg@nombro
        \@ifundefined{pglasta@\the\pg@nombro}{}%
          {\bookmark[level=2,page=\the\pg@nombro]%
            {\csname pglasta@\the\pg@nombro\endcsname}}%
      \else
        \@ifundefined{pgunesma@\the\pg@nombro}{}%
          {\bookmark[level=2,page=\the\pg@nombro]%
            {\csname pgunesma@\the\pg@nombro\endcsname}}%
      \fi
    \repeat}}
\makeatother

\begin{document}
\signeti
% The first three pages of the bound book: the front cover, its blank
% verso, the title page. The verso of the title stays blank too, and the
% dictionary begins on a recto, as in printed books -- \cleardoublepage
% lays the next page on an odd number.
\platrekto
\cleardoublepage
\titolpagino
\cleardoublepage

\small
\input{content}
% Final flyleaf, laid on a recto by \cleardoublepage.
\cleardoublepage
\thispagestyle{empty}
\null
\clearpage
% A book is counted in EVEN pages: each leaf carries two faces, and an odd
% total would leave one face orphaned at the binding. The back cover takes
% the last page, and must therefore fall on an EVEN one. After the
% \clearpage above, the counter points at the page the back cover will
% take; if it is odd, a flyleaf is slipped in.
\ifodd\value{page}
  \thispagestyle{empty}\null\clearpage
\fi
\platverso
\end{document}
